_employment_history_companies_note: INDUSTRY EMPLOYERS ONLY — companies you were formally employed by (on payroll). EXCLUDES academic/university research positions, lab affiliations, and student clubs (e.g. FSU CISCOR lab research, Carnegie Mellon Racing are NOT employment). This list's completeness is what makes the auto-'No' to 'previously employed here?' safe — keep it accurate and complete. NOT derived from work_experience; maintain it by hand. An empty list [] is treated as UNFILLED and will flag every such question for manual review. If you have genuinely never been formally employed in industry, set this to ["none"] to auto-answer 'No'. These names are ALSO matched against the QUESTION TEXT itself, which often names the entities that count (affiliates/subsidiaries/predecessors, e.g. "Elavon, U.S. Bancorp Investments, or Union Bank") — so list the specific legal-entity names you were employed by, not just a parent brand; a known employer named in the question fills 'Yes' (always flagged for review).

personal_info._country_fields_note: country and country_phone_code take a TIERED candidate list (most-specific first), not a plain string, because the rendered Workday option text differs from the everyday value: the country dropdown shows "United States of America" and the phone-code typeahead shows "United States of America (+1)". Listing the exact option text first yields a high-confidence EXACT match; a bare "United States" only containment-matches (medium confidence). A plain string still works for both. This tiered form is NOT needed for most fields — only ones whose rendered option text differs from the natural value.

education._degree_field_of_study_note: degree and field_of_study are CHOICE fields (dropdown / typeahead) whose option text varies by tenant, so give each an ORDERED, most-specific-first candidate list ending in a safe fallback — the filler tries them in order and takes the first match (same tiered model as personal_info.country). A plain string still works. Example: degree: ["Bachelor of Science", "Bachelor's Degree", "Bachelors"] (many Workday dropdowns only offer "Bachelors"); field_of_study: ["Electrical and Computer Engineering", "Other", "computer engineering", "electrical engineering"]. Keep these tiers in the PROFILE — the filler is generic.

_languages_note: Each language has per-skill proficiency (reading/speaking/writing) — the Workday Languages section has a separate required dropdown for each. Use the rendered option text (this tenant: Advanced/Basic/Fluent/Intermediate/None); like degree, a value MAY be a tiered most-specific-first array if a tenant's vocabulary differs. `language` must match an option in the Language dropdown (e.g. "English", "Chinese"). If a language or proficiency can't match an option, the engine deletes that (optional) entry rather than block submit.
_certifications_note: Top-level certifications fill the Workday Certifications section (separate from application_questions.role_specific.certifications). `certification` is a typeahead PICK from the tenant's list — give it the exact option text (string, or a tiered most-specific-first array like degree). Dates are FULL `YYYY-MM-DD`; a partial (`YYYY-MM`) or placeholder date is skipped (not half-filled). An entry whose `certification` can't match an option is DROPPED (delete-on-no-match) rather than blocking submit, since the section is optional.
_consent_override_note: Structural consents (terms_and_conditions_acceptance, truthfulness_certification) default to True via the schema's auto_accept rule when left null/empty here. Setting one to literal false overrides to False AND surfaces in <page>_review.json — used if you intend not to consent and not submit. Other agreements (personal_data_statement_consent, background_check_consent, drug_alcohol_test_consent) are real choices: leave null to skip, true to fill, false to refuse.
